paper.title_en: Theory for the Rydberg states of helium: Quantum defect extensions and comparison with experiment up to <math><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>102</mn></mrow></math> for the singlet and triplet <math><mi>P</mi></math> states
paper.abstract_en: High-precision variational calculations for helium in Hylleraas coordinates are used to obtain a combination of quantum defect expansions for the nonrelativistic energy and <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>n</mi></mrow></math> expansions for the relativistic and quantum electrodynamic corrections. The extrapolations based on direct calculations for the singlet and triplet <math><mi>P</mi></math> states up to principal quantum number <math><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>35</mn></mrow></math> provide ionization energies of the <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>s</mi><mi>n</mi><mi>p</mi><mspace width="0.16em"/><mmultiscripts><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>1</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> and <math><mmultiscripts><mi>P</mi><mi>c</mi><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>3</mn></mmultiscripts></math> (centroid) states up to <math><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>102</mn></mrow></math> with accuracies better than <math><mrow><mo>±</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math> kHz. The calculated ionization energies are combined with 28 measured transition frequencies to obtain values for the ionization energy of the <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn><mi>s</mi><mspace width="0.16em"/><mmultiscripts><mi>S</mi><mn>1</mn><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>3</mn></mmultiscripts></mrow></math> state. The final result of 1 152 842 742.705(16) MHz differs from theory by <math><mrow><mn>0.474</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.052</mn></mrow></math> MHz, and provides a strong confirmation of the <math><mrow><mn>9</mn><mi>σ</mi></mrow></math> disagreement between theory and experiment obtained previously by quantum defect extrapolation of experimental data to the series limit. An analysis of the quantum defect method is presented, and second-order mass polarization (recoil) terms are identified that vary as <math><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></math> in lowest order. The nonrelativistic part provides a theoretical justification for the effective reduced-mass Rydberg <math><msubsup><mi>R</mi><mi>M</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mo>+</mo><mo>)</mo></mrow></msubsup></math> based on the phenomenological model of a Rydberg electron scattering from a <math><msup><mrow><mi>He</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo></msup></math> core. The Ritz expansion for the nonrelativistic energy is verified to 20-figure accuracy.
